text:
maria: Quick heads-up from last night's bring-up of carina-6b-int4 on GTN replay. S3 snapshot: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/carina6b/2026-03-22/summary.json TL;DR: ~46% per-token compute saving vs int6 on our sample workload, but we observed a ~2.7% drop in QA exact-match on the GTN subset and a handful of hallucination cases for >2k token contexts. Need quick recs: canary %, fallback, and routing strategy for product and GTN.

alex: can you paste the slice breakdown? overall numbers are useful but we need by-intent and by-context-length.

maria: upload is in the snapshot above. quick numbers: overall EM 0.923 -> 0.899 (drop 2.7 pts), latency median 120ms -> 95ms, p95 470ms -> 330ms, cost/unit ~46% lower. long-context (>2048) EM drop larger ~6.2 pts.

devon: sounds like classic quant cliff on long context. my quick recos: 1) hybrid routing by context length (int6 for >1024 tokens), 2) enable prefix/KV cache sticky routing so multi-turn sessions stick to int6 if warmed, 3) canary at 5% with shadowing to compare EM for slices. sample routing flag we'd use:```json
{
  "routing": {
    "strategy": "length_based_hybrid",
    "threshold_tokens": 1024,
    "fallback_model": "carina-6b-int6",
    "canary_percent": 5
  }
}
```

sam: agree with devon. I'd start 5% for 24h with slice monitors (QA EM, hallucination rate, latency/cost). If EM delta <1pt after 24-48h, ramp to 30% and keep KV-cache sticky. Also recommend a temporary traffic-split rule: 10% of high-risk intents always to int6 (search, code, finance), rest hybrid.

alex: request: add the failing prompt examples to the ticket so product/GTN can inspect. also we should test per-layer outlier-clipping quant config (we did that briefly — small win on stability).

maria: here's one repro prompt (sensitive long-context case):```
User: "Summarize the below conversation and extract action items"
[~3.5k tokens of earlier chat omitted]
Assistant: <fabricated dates and facts>
```
This pattern shows up on 8 sessions in the GTN slice.

devon: on quant side we can try two things in parallel: per-layer 8-bit compensation (reduce outlier corruption) and a light mixed-precision variant (keep first/last n layers at int6). both add ~10-12% cost vs pure int4 but recover most of the long-context EM. would run both as A/B shadows.

sam: operational ask: can we have deploy-bot start a 5% canary with shadowing to int6 for metrics? also add alerts for EM delta >1.5pt on any critical slice.

deploy-bot: Canary started: carina-6b-int4 @ 5% traffic; shadowing enabled to carina-6b-int6 for full-sample comparison. Monitoring hooks: gtn_em, hallucination_rate, latency_p95.

alex: I'll open GH ticket infra/eng-ml#1234 with the snapshot, failing examples, and evaluation checklist (512/1024/2k slices, per-intent). assign to @devon + @maria.

maria: thanks. timeline: we'll run 24h canary then a 48h mixed-precision shadow if the 5% shows the long-context problem persists. product: are we OK with initial 5%? @sam?

sam: yes from product side. 5% is fine. will notify GTN and prepare rollback playbook. :thumbsup:

alex: one more note — run a quick priming test (1000 examples) with heavy long-context and measure token-level entropy; might reveal where quantization introduces noise.

maria: good call. I've queued the priming test now, will post results to the ticket.

sam: thanks all. keep the updates short in the ticket thread, no need to spam here.

maria: will do. ping me if you want the raw logs.

(emoji reactions: :thumbsup: on deploy-bot message, :eyes: on devon comment)
